shouldFix.title: The historical honesty-block declaration still lags the current block by one generation: v12 adds honestyRepairsFromV11 but declares only honestyRepairsFromV1 through honestyRepairsFromV9 historical, leaving honestyRepairsFromV10 outside the declared range.
evidence: signed-index-trust-contract.v12 carries honestyRepairsFromV1 through honestyRepairsFromV11. honestyRepairsFromV11 is the new current block recording the v11-to-v12 work, so honestyRepairsFromV10 is now a predecessor block.

The frozen unlabeled Codex v11 honesty-block finding states the lineage rule directly: once honestyRepairsFromV10 existed as the current block in v11, honestyRepairsFromV9 was historical and the declaration had to advance through V9. Applying the same rule after v12 creates honestyRepairsFromV11 makes V10 historical.

v12 correctly restores honestyRepairsFromV9 byte-for-byte from frozen signed-index-trust-contract.v10 and preserves honestyRepairsFromV10 byte-for-byte from frozen signed-index-trust-contract.v11. There is no current historical-block mutation. The defect is that basedOn.method and the current honestyRepairsFromV11[1] record both stop the protected historical range at V9 rather than V10.

The prompt-enumerated v11 repair therefore lands literally, but the act of adding the V11 block advances the provenance boundary one further step. Without that advance, the immediate predecessor block is again the only old block not explicitly classified historical.
shouldFix.whyItMatters: The historical declaration is the lineage's protection against rewriting predecessor repair records. Leaving the immediately preceding block outside that range recreates the same one-generation lag that permitted the V8 and V9 block mutations, even though v12 does not itself mutate V10. This is provenance incompleteness, not a defect in the DR-112 design body or the closed successor roster.
shouldFix.severityBasis: SHOULD-FIX rather than MUST-FIX because honestyRepairsFromV10 is currently byte-identical to its frozen v11 introduction bytes, all 30 v11-to-v12 changed paths are covered by the Closed roster, and no byte-equality claim is false. The declaration should nevertheless match the block that is actually current before acceptance.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Advance both the basedOn.method historical sentence and honestyRepairsFromV11[1] from honestyRepairsFromV1 through honestyRepairsFromV9 to honestyRepairsFromV1 through honestyRepairsFromV10. Do not modify honestyRepairsFromV1 through honestyRepairsFromV10; the existing /basedOn and /honestyRepairsFromV11 roster tokens already cover the two sentence edits.
shouldFix.notRequested: Do not alter the restored honestyRepairsFromV9 bytes, mutate honestyRepairsFromV10, change the Closed roster paths, mark any register row SATISFIED, mint an OD-112 identifier, or choose the residual Preview refuse axis.
